title: Lafayette Cartee survey maps
description: LaFayette Cartee came to Idaho in 1863, the year President Abraham Lincoln established the territory. In 1866, President Andrew Johnson nominated Cartee to serve as Idaho’s first Surveyor General. For over a decade, he oversaw the surveying of Idaho, providing insight into the evolving story of the region’s land and people. Cartee's surveying work resulted in the creation of these maps.
identifier_old: G4271.S1. "Cartee Survey of Idaho." 1867. Idaho State Archives.
